title: Commands and lambdas
summary: startEnd, runOnce, and handing over code to run later.

say.never: A **lambda** is a tiny method with no name, written `() -> ...`. The key idea: you're *not running it now*. You're handing it over so something else can run it later, like giving someone a note that says "when I press this button, do this".
say.bit: `() -> ...` is a tiny method with no name. You're not running it now: you're handing it over to run later.

say.never: `startEnd` builds a command out of two notes. The first lambda runs when the command **starts** (here: turn the lights on). The second runs when it **ends** (turn them off). When you let go of the button, the command ends.
say.bit: `Commands.startEnd(start, end, requirements)` runs one lambda when the command starts and another when it ends.

say.never: `startEnd` builds a command out of two notes. The first lambda runs when the command **starts** (here: tell the shooter to SHOOT). The second runs when it **ends** (here: tell it to go back to IDLE). When you let go of the button, the command ends.
say.bit: `startEnd` runs one lambda when the command starts and another when it ends.
